seoTitle: Keyword Transliteration: Cyrillic, Greek and Kana to Latin Letters
metaDescription: Turn Russian, Ukrainian, Greek and Japanese kana keywords into Latin spellings and URL slugs with simple rules. Free, in your browser.
intro: Converts keywords written in Cyrillic (Russian or Ukrainian), Greek or Japanese hiragana and katakana into Latin letters, with an optional URL slug.
why:
People often type foreign-language queries with Latin letters, and URL slugs in Latin letters are easier to share. A rule-based romanization gives you a quick first version of both.

These are simplified rules, not official standards, and I did not check them against the standard texts, so do not use them for passports or legal names. Kanji and Chinese characters cannot be converted without a dictionary and are left unchanged. Chinese pinyin is not supported. Always check real search queries in Search Console.
howTo: Paste your keywords, one per line.
Tick the slug option if you need URL forms.
Check the result with a native speaker for important pages.

faq.a: Pinyin needs a dictionary of thousands of characters, with several readings per character. It is not included.
None strictly. Russian is close to BGN/PCGN, Ukrainian follows the common national scheme with initial and medial forms, Japanese follows Hepburn without macrons.
Yes, accents are stripped before converting.

faq.q: Should URLs be in Latin letters?
faq.a: Google handles non-Latin URLs, but Latin slugs are easier to share and to type. Choose by audience.
